encounters.cc: Gradually worsening shortness of breath over several months with dry, persistent cough, initially noticed when climbing hills or carrying groceries.

lines: Gradually worsening shortness of breath over several months with dry, persistent cough, initially noticed when climbing hills or carrying groceries.
She notices it most when she climbs the small hill behind her house.
She describes a dry, persistent cough that interrupts conversations.
The cough began months ago and has become more frequent.
She denies chest pain at rest.
She feels winded when carrying groceries from the car.
She has started taking shorter walks in the evening.
She sleeps with an extra pillow for comfort.
She has not had night sweats.
She has noticed mild, unintentional weight loss.
She has noticed a faint blue-gray tint on sun-exposed areas.
She sometimes sees halos around lights at night.
She denies rash aside from photosensitivity.
Lately the story feels short of breath.
She pauses halfway up her driveway.
She stops to breathe after making the bed.
She misses finishing sentences without a breath.
She has tried over-the-counter cough remedies.
Over the past six months, breathing has become her main worry.
She says talking about clouds now makes her cough.
She cancelled a planned lecture on frontal dynamics last week.
Walking across a breezy parking lot leaves her winded.
She feels a tight band across the lower chest when she exerts.
She denies swelling in her ankles.
She has not changed detergents or soaps.
She has not started new medications except occasional acetaminophen.
She has no recent travel to high elevations.
She still enjoys watching cold air damming events.
She notes that inversions have been frequent this winter.
She says smoke from distant fires drifted in last summer.
Her symptoms began before that season.
- Congestive heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
She has a history of atrial fibrillation.
Her arrhythmia was diagnosed two years ago.
She was started on amiodarone after several emergency visits.
She once had pneumonia as a teenager.
She had no lung problems for decades.
She did not seek evaluation at that time.
She had a chest image a year ago for palpitations.
She has been taking the same amiodarone daily since diagnosis.
- Warfarin 5 mg daily, adjusted per INR
Her father had emphysema from heavy smoking. Her mother has seasonal allergies.
She has no known occupational dust exposure.
She has never worked in mines.
She has never sandblasted or cut stone.
She drinks wine socially on weekends.
She has no pets at home.
She teaches a community class on weather and climate.
She keeps a cloud journal on her porch.
Cumulus clouds make her think of scattered thoughts that build through the day.
Cumulonimbus towers remind her of summer drama.
Stratus decks feel to her like a blanket that quiets the town.
She watches cirrus filaments for hints of change.
She listens for shifts in wind from sea breeze to land breeze.
She teaches students how fronts shape the sky.
El Niño years energize her conversations.
La Niña years sharpen her forecasts.
She distinguishes maritime tropical air from continental polar air with ease.
She sketches jet stream meanders on napkins.
She compares trade winds to steady routines.
She calls gust fronts the breath of summer storms.
She times the arrival of a cold front by smell and feel.
Her neighbors ask her when to cover their gardens.
She tracks barometer trends like plot twists.
She photographs Kelvin-Helmholtz waves when rare.
She points out mammatus beneath anvils after sunset.
She notes fallstreak holes with quiet delight.
She follows Saharan dust plumes across the ocean on maps.
She explains atmospheric rivers to curious children.
She teaches that maritime polar air feels raw and clean.
She contrasts continental tropical air as heavy and hazy.
She says weather is a story the sky tells.
Chest x-ray shows reticulonodularity with honeycombing.
Spirometry shows a restrictive lung pattern.

encounters.cc: Two-day history of nausea, vomiting, decreased appetite, and visual disturbances described as seeing 'halos' around lights.

lines: Two-day history of nausea, vomiting, decreased appetite, and visual disturbances described as seeing 'halos' around lights.

This 69-year-old female with atrial fibrillation, congestive heart failure, and prior amiodarone-induced pulmonary toxicity and thyrotoxicosis presents with two-day nausea, vomiting, decreased appetite, and visual disturbances.
She also reports seeing "halos" around lights.
- Congestive heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
Her medications include digoxin, warfarin, and furosemide.
She was recently started on amiodarone for recurrent atrial fibrillation.
Alcohol: Social, 2-3 glasses of wine on weekends.
Her blood pressure is 130/80 mmHg, heart rate is 60 beats per minute, and respiratory rate is 16 breaths per minute.
Physical examination is unremarkable except for mild bilateral pedal edema.
- Serum digoxin level: 2.5 ng/mL (normal range: 0.5-2.0 ng/mL)
An ECG shows normal sinus rhythm with occasional premature ventricular contractions.

encounters.cc: Sudden onset severe pain in the right eye and blurred vision beginning 4 hours ago, associated with nausea and vomiting.

lines: Sudden onset severe pain in the right eye and blurred vision beginning 4 hours ago, associated with nausea and vomiting.

The patient is a 70-year-old female with atrial fibrillation, congestive heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, Parkinson's disease, and prior amiodarone-induced pulmonary toxicity, thyrotoxicosis, and digoxin toxicity who presents to the emergency department with a 4-hour history of sudden onset severe right eye pain and blurred vision.
She also reports nausea and vomiting.
- Congestive heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
- Warfarin 5 mg daily, adjusted per INR
Alcohol: Social, 2-3 glasses of wine on weekends.
On examination, her right eye is red with conjunctival injection, the cornea appears hazy, and the pupil is mid-dilated and non-reactive to light.
Visual acuity is decreased in the affected eye.
Intraocular pressure (IOP) of the right eye is measured at 48 mmHg, while the left eye has an IOP of 14 mmHg.
Fundoscopic examination is difficult due to corneal edema.

lines: Acute onset of palpitations and light-headedness beginning 2 hours ago, with hemodynamic instability.

On examination, her blood pressure is 130/85 mmHg, heart rate is 150 beats per minute and irregular, and respiratory rate is 18 breaths per minute.
- Serum digoxin level: 1.5 ng/mL (normal therapeutic range: 0.5-2.0 ng/mL)

encounters.cc: Sudden acute shortness of breath, chest pain, and lightheadedness occurring while walking to the bathroom.

lines: Sudden acute shortness of breath, chest pain, and lightheadedness occurring while walking to the bathroom.

This 72-year-old female with atrial fibrillation, heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, and a history of amiodarone-induced pulmonary toxicity, thyrotoxicosis, and digoxin toxicity presents with acute cardiopulmonary complaints.
She reports that her symptoms started suddenly while she was walking to the bathroom.
- Congestive heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
Recent total hip replacement surgery 4 days ago
Alcohol: Social, 2-3 glasses of wine on weekends.
Blood pressure is 85/50 mmHg, heart rate is 110 bpm, respiratory rate is 28 breaths/min, and oxygen saturation is 89% on room air
Lung auscultation reveals no crackles, and there is no leg swelling or tenderness.
An ECG shows a new-onset right bundle branch block.
